replication.target_description: Chinese communication scholars’ SEM of attitudes and behavioral intentions toward data sharing; row-specific path unresolved from generic description.

notes: Identity independently verified from title page: Attitudinal, Normative, and Resource Factors Affecting Communication Scholars’ Data Sharing: A Replication Study; Jinghong Xu and Rukun Zhang; Media and Communication, 2024, Volume 12, Article 7666; DOI 10.17645/mac.7666. Supplied canonical text is a full primary research article with methods, results, discussion, references and author biographies, not an abstract or secondary article. No PDF was supplied. Original side and unassigned fields are placeholders only. Candidate standardized SEM paths (Figure 3, pp. 9–11): perceived benefit → attitudes beta .544, p < .001; perceived risk → attitudes beta −.116, p < .05; perceived effort → attitudes beta −.159, p < .001; perceived effort → behavioral intentions beta −.022, p > .05; attitudes → behavioral intentions beta .565, p < .001 (Figure 3); subjective norms → behavioral intentions beta .169, p < .001; journal pressure → behavioral intentions beta .197, prose p > .001 but Figure 3 p < .001; facilitating conditions → behavioral intentions beta .094, p < .05. Figure 3 explicitly identifies standardized path coefficients. Generic description does not distinguish these paths. No targets assigned by row order or numeric values. Common final-model participant N candidate = 351, explicitly reported after removal of 61 responses (20 fast responses ≤ 361.3 seconds and 41 slow responses ≥ 1431 seconds) from 412 responses. Pilot N=30 and sampling-frame N=871 are separate roles. N is retained only as candidate because row-specific test is unresolved; no N arithmetic or summation performed. Authors describe agreements and disagreements with the original, but the row-specific replication verdict cannot be established.
